draft.title: Statements and connectives
card: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false, such as 7 is prime. A question or an instruction is not a proposition.
And
P and Q is true only when both P and Q are true.
Or
P or Q is true when at least one of P and Q is true. It is false only when both are false.
Not
not P has the opposite truth value to P. A truth table lists every true and false case. With two propositions there are 4 rows. A Karnaugh map shows the same cases in a grid.
draft.remember: And needs both true. Or needs at least one true. Not flips the value.

a.q: P is true and Q is false. Which compound statement is true?
a.why: Or is true when at least one part is true, and P is true. P and Q fails because Q is false. not P is false, so not P and Q is also false.
a.clue: Which connective only needs one true part?

b.q: Today is not raining (P is false) and it is windy (Q is true). Which statement about the day is true?
b.why: not P is true because P is false, and Q is true, so not P and Q is true. P or not Q is false, since both P and not Q are false. P and Q is false because P is false. not Q or P is false since both parts are false.
b.clue: Work out the value of not P and not Q first.

problems.detail: 'not P and Q' is ambiguous because the card never says that not applies only to the letter right after it. Read as not (P and Q), it is true when P is true and Q is false, so a second option can be defended. Use brackets, for example (not P) and Q.
'Today is not raining (P is false)' never says what P stands for. A student could take P to mean 'it is not raining'. Say 'P: it is raining. Today it is not raining, so P is false.'

check.summary: Both intended answers are correct. In question a, 'not P and Q' needs brackets, because read as not (P and Q) it is also true. Question b should say what P stands for.

proposal.title: Statements and connectives
card: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false, such as 7 is prime. A truth table, or a grid called a Karnaugh map, shows when a compound statement is true in every case.
And
P and Q is true only when both P and Q are true.
Or
P or Q is true when at least one of P and Q is true. It is false only when both are false.
Not
not P has the opposite truth value to P. Brackets show what not applies to: (not P) and Q is not the same as not (P and Q).
proposal.remember: And needs both true. Or needs at least one true. Not flips the value.

a.q: P is true and Q is false. Which compound statement is true?
a.why: Or is true when at least one part is true, and P is true. P and Q fails because Q is false. not P is false, so (not P) and Q is also false.
a.clue: Which connective only needs one true part?

b.q: P: it is raining. Q: it is windy. Today it is not raining, so P is false, and it is windy, so Q is true. Which statement is true?
b.why: not P is true because P is false, and Q is true, so (not P) and Q is true. not (P or Q) is tempting, but P or Q is true because Q is true, so its opposite is false. P or (not Q) and P and Q are both false.
b.clue: Work out what is inside each bracket first.
